final_answer:
Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that works by recursively splitting a list into halves until each sublist has one element. Then, it merges the sublists back together in a sorted manner. During the merging step, the algorithm compares the first elements of each sublist and takes the smaller one, appending it to the result. This continues until all elements are merged.

Merge sort is preferred over quicksort for linked lists because linked lists have poor random access performance. Quicksort relies heavily on accessing elements at arbitrary positions, which is inefficient for linked lists. Merge sort, on the other hand, can efficiently perform its merge step with linked lists, as it only requires sequential access. Additionally, merge sort is a stable sort, which can be beneficial in certain cases. Thus, merge sort is better suited for linked lists due to its efficient merging and stable nature, even though both algorithms have similar average time complexities.
